edges.description: An interval that includes SIM1 removes one genomic copy.
An interval that includes POU3F2 removes one genomic copy.
More proximal deletions can remove all or part of EPHA7.
Several deletion intervals associate with developmental impairment; deleted-gene contributions and intervening cellular events differ.
A SIM1-containing 6q16.1-q21 deletion was associated with later pituitary deficiency. The responsible gene and anatomical lesion were not established in this case.
Reduced functional dosage is supported by loss-of-function variant assays, but SIM1 target transcription has not been directly measured in the deletion-carrier hypothalamus.
Genetic association with obesity and experimental loss of transcriptional activity support a contribution to appetite regulation, with unresolved human neuronal intermediates.

Intragenic-variant assays support altered transcriptional function as a consequence of POU3F2 disruption. Individual DNA-binding and activation effects vary, and are not direct measurements in deletion carriers.
POU3F2-containing deletions and separate intragenic variants associate with hyperphagia and obesity; the responsible human target genes and neural-circuit changes remain unresolved.
Human POU3F2 disruption is associated with neurodevelopmental impairment, but the intermediate cellular effects have not been established by the available deletion evidence.
Clinical deletion data support a susceptibility relationship; specific human cellular intermediates remain unknown.
The clinical appetite phenotype is compatible with disturbed regulation, but a specific neural satiety defect has not been measured in deletion carriers.
Obesity susceptibility is variable; energy intake, expenditure and other contributors were not comprehensively measured in the deletion cohorts.
Multi-domain delay is documented clinically; its cellular basis is unresolved.
Cognitive impairment is reported in overlapping deletion cohorts, without a resolved common cellular mediator.
Language delay is a documented component of the variable neurodevelopmental phenotype; the responsible neural intermediates remain unresolved.
Delayed acquisition of walking is a motor-developmental manifestation in the detailed SIM1-sparing case; a specific central motor lesion has not been established.
Autistic features are documented in the SIM1-sparing case, without a standardized autism diagnosis or a resolved cellular pathway.
Clinical cohorts support behavioral involvement as part of the neurodevelopmental spectrum, with heterogeneous deletion content and incompletely identified mediators.
Hypotonia accompanies developmental impairment in some deletion carriers. A central developmental contribution is plausible but not localized by the available clinical evidence.
Some EPHA7-containing deletion carriers have postnatal microcephaly. The association with altered neurodevelopment is clinically supported without a demonstrated human cellular growth mechanism.
Directly assays SIM1-dependent reporter activation.
edges.limitations: Engineered non-neuronal cells testing intragenic variants, not a patient-derived deletion model; reporter loss does not identify the relevant human hypothalamic target or prove a neuronal developmental lesion.
